title: which consumer actually reads the identity a study face declares
population_source: the graded rows of E458's faceidentity_latest.json that declare a top-level machine-readable identity; the .py corpus is e451.walk_py minus this study's own files
method_limits: static: a consumer is a source that names the face and reads the declared field name; a consumer that reaches the field through a variable key (d[k] where k = 'stu'+'dy') is invisible
a source 'names' a face when a string constant in it normalises to the face stem, so a name composed from parts is missed (same bound E458 publishes)
value join requires the literal value in the consumer's source; a consumer that compares against a constant defined in another module is counted as a field join only
read/write is decided by the AST context of the key constant, not by data flow: a dict literal built to be returned is graded a write even if a caller reads it back
